chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated, from ʿAlī ibn Khālid, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who sleeps through the fajr until the sun rises while he is on a journey—what should he do? Is it permissible for him to make it up during the day? He said: He should not make up, during the day, either a nafilah prayer or an obligatory prayer; it is not permissible for him, nor is it established for him. Rather, he should delay it and then make it up at night.

So this is an anomalous report, which is not to be used in opposition to the reports that we have presented earlier, along with their accordance with the apparent meaning of the Book and the consensus of the Ummah.

key_terms.إِجْمَاعِ الْأُمَّةِ: the consensus of the Muslim community
key_terms.خَبَرٌ شَاذٌّ: an anomalous report not relied upon against stronger evidence
key_terms.ظَاهِرِ الْكِتَابِ: the apparent meaning of the Qur'an
key_terms.فِي سَفَرٍ: while being in a state of travel
key_terms.يَقْضِيَ: to perform a missed prayer as qaḍāʾ

ai.seo_question: Can a traveler who misses fajr make it up during the daytime according to this hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on making up fajr after sunrise for a traveler who slept through it. The compiler then states that this narration is anomalous and cannot oppose the other reports that accord with the apparent meaning of the Qur'an and the consensus of the Ummah.
